gpu: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (16 GiB GDDR6, 64 CUs, Wave32)
changes: qwen3 architecture: per-head q/k RMSNorm (qk_rmsnorm_f32) before RoPE, key_length head_dim, Q6_K embedding lookup for tied Qwen3-4B token_embd
Q4_K decode GEMV row scaling (gemv_q4_k_r4/r8_f32): rows per workgroup grow as k/256 shrinks so all 16 superblock groups stay busy (Qwen3-4B nb=10 was 62.5% idle)
hipGraph decode capture: device-resident pos slot (rope/kv_append/gqa_attn read *pos), decode_advance_u32 epilogue (token <- argmax, pos += 1), one graph replay per token
prefill WMMA 64x128 macro-tile with 4 accumulators/wave (gemm_wmma_*), dispatched when >=128 blocks are available; 32x64 tile kept for small matrices
scoria graph-soak: 1000-replay hipMemGetInfo leak guard for the decode graph

parity.method: scripts/parity_oracle.py vs libllama.so b11050, llama.cpp CPU reference
parity.note: 5-token prompts (m<8, FP32 scalar GEMM path) sit at cos ~0.9983 on the 7B because llama.cpp quantises activations to Q8_K for Q4_K matmul while scoria keeps FP32; greedy tokens still match exactly.

qwen3-4b-instruct-2507-q4_k_m.note: hipMemGetInfo is process-global; drift tracks VRAM held by other GPU clients and stays far under the 64 MiB guard

remaining_gap.decode: Weights are streamed ~492 GB/s on the 8B (5.02 GB/step) vs a 561.66 GB/s measured stream ceiling; lm_head alone reaches ~600 GB/s on the same kernel, so the loss is per-layer launch/fill work rather than raw GEMV.
remaining_gap.prefill: pp128 has a ~25 ms per-forward constant: Q4_K GEMV fill re-reads the 16 B superblock header once per BK=32 step (8x per 256-weight block) and each weight is read twice at BM=64 with m=128. Marginal rate beyond that constant is ~4165 tok/s on the 8B.
